title: Port fly, build a 3D scroll widget, ship /resume/

set.tab: Port fly directory and a… - monorepo - Visual Studio Code
set.request: Port C:/Code/lew42com/public/fly/ into this repo; find the 3D scroll demo and build a similar widget for this site; create /public/resume/ from a rough draft and add the 3D scroll effect to it, subtly — headings closer to the camera, h1 deepest, h2 sections as nested bg cards, and a depth slider factoring all depths.
steps: Link Fly + Resume from the home page
Verify — fly runs, resume measured at 4 widths
set.outcome:
**Three deliverables, all linked from the home page's sidebar and card wall.** [/fly/](/fly/) — the three.js flight sim ported standalone, three r0.181.2 vendored into the dir with its bare specifiers rewritten. [/framework/ext/depth/](/framework/ext/depth/) — the 3D scroll as a reusable ext, declared in ext's children, with readme, Doc page, four doc/file notes and doc/method/depth.md. [/resume/](/resume/) — the résumé on the draft, and the ext's showcase: name closest at depth 4, section cards at 2 with their h2s at 3, and a slider that factors every depth.

Three silent bugs found by measuring rather than looking: ext/depth never set --depth-focus on load (page still display:none for both the microtask and the first rAF); the fly canvas was sized before device metrics settled and framework.css's `max-width: 100%` then clamped its width while leaving the tall inline height, squishing the view and putting the plane below the joystick; and the joystick knob sat 50px low because `:first-child { margin-top: 0 }` lives in @layer util. All three now fixed by construction — ResizeObservers instead of one-shots, grid centring instead of negative margins.

Still open: the résumé's placeholder email and phone.
